human_tolerance.notes: Since the 1950s raccoons have lived in large North American cities; in towns and suburbs they sleep in garden tree hollows, garages and attics and forage on garden fruit, insects and waste. Urban home ranges are only 3-40 ha for females and 8-80 ha for males.

phases.name: mating
phases.note: Mating is triggered by increasing daylight between late January and mid-March, later in the southern states.

phases.name: young
phases.note: Gestation is usually 63-65 days; a litter of typically two to five kits is weaned by about 16 weeks and the juvenile group splits up in the fall.

phases.name: caching
phases.note: Late-summer and autumn fruits and nuts are eaten heavily to build the fat stores for winter.

vocalizations.description: A rapid series of chirps and whistles given while feeding or moving together; one of the most social of the raccoon's calls.
A low, rumbling growl used when threatened or in a dispute over food, often with the body hunched and the fur raised.
A piercing shriek, most often heard in fights between males during the mating season and sometimes mistaken for a bird or a human cry.
A soft, high whine and purr-like sound exchanged between a mother and her kits.

range.note: Native throughout North America from southern Canada to Panama, so the country list covers the continental range; the island forms (Bahamas, Guadeloupe, Tres Marias) are omitted as extinct or endangered. Introduced by escapes and releases in Germany, northern France, Spain, Italy, Belarus, Azerbaijan and Japan; Germany and Japan are the established populations treated as invasive/problematic. Country codes are ISO 3166-1 alpha-2.

traits.locomotion_modes.note: Plantigrade walker with a top speed of 16-24 km/h, and an unusual ability to climb down a tree headfirst by rotating the hind feet; judgement mapping to Walk, Trot and Climb.

traits.nest_type.note: Tree hollows in old oaks and rock crevices are preferred as sleeping, winter and litter dens; burrows of other mammals, dense undergrowth and tree crotches are used when hollows are unavailable.

traits.perching.note: Climbs and rests in tree crotches, but does not perch like a bird; set to false.

traits.mass_kg.note: Midpoint of the usual adult range of 5-12 kg; the species spans 2-26 kg, and males are 15-20% heavier than females.

traits.mass_range_kg.note: The usual adult range given as 5-12 kg; the full recorded range is 2-26 kg.

traits.length_m.note: Head to hindquarters 40-70 cm plus a tail of 20-40 cm, midpoints summed to 85 cm.

traits.shoulder_height_m.note: Midpoint of the stated 23-30 cm shoulder height.

traits.lifespan_y.note: Wikidata P2250 gives 1.8-3.1 years in the wild (2.45 used); Wikipedia adds that captive animals have lived more than 20 years.

traits.home_range_ha.note: Urban home ranges are 3-40 ha for females and 8-80 ha for males; 20 ha is a judgement within that band. Rural home ranges are far larger (2-50 km2).

traits.diet.note: From the stated diet of about 40% invertebrates, 33% plant material and 27% vertebrates; the plant share is split into fruit (20) and mast (13) as judgement, since the article does not break it down.

traits.social.note: Set to Solitary with a single-animal group: related females form fission-fusion societies and unrelated males loose groups of up to four, which the schema's single structure and group_size do not model.

traits.activity_pattern.note: 'Though usually nocturnal, the raccoon is sometimes active in daylight to take advantage of available food sources.'

traits.defense.note: Climbs a tree or retreats to a den when threatened; judgement mapping to the schema's single-value field.

traits.wariness.note: Judgement: urban raccoons are bold around houses and waste, but warier where hunted.

habitat.use.note: Judgement: forages mainly on the ground but climbs to dens, fruit and escape routes; raccoons avoid open terrain because they need vertical structures to climb.

habitat.resources.note: Food weights follow traits.diet. Nesting and shelter weights are judgement; water is included because lakeside and marsh habitats sustain the highest densities.

habitat.human_tolerance.note: From the 'Urban raccoons' section: city populations since the 1950s, dens in garden trees and attics, and garden fruit, insects and waste as food.

habitat.density_per_ha.note: Converted from the stated 0.5-3.2 animals/km2 in prairies, up to 6/km2 in upland hardwood forest, and 50-150/km2 in the densest urban areas; typical is a judgement between the rural and urban figures.

seasonal.strategy.note: Active year-round in the south; in the northern part of the range raccoons enter a winter rest while permanent snow covers the ground.

seasonal.phases.note: Mating window, gestation and weaning timings are from the Reproduction section; the autumn caching window is judgement, tied to the late-summer and autumn fruit and nut diet.

seasonal.life_stages.note: Kits are weaned by about 16 weeks (120 days used) and the juvenile group splits up in the fall; the 0.5 scale is authored judgement.

vocalizations.note: The raccoon has thirteen identified calls; the four here (chitter, growl, scream, whine) are described qualitatively in the article's communication text. Time windows and cooldowns are authored judgement, as no open source quantifies them.

look.note: Grizzled grey-brown fur, pale face border with the black bandit mask around the eyes, ringed tail and short legs, from the Description section; proportions and the extra mask part are authored judgement.

behavior.note: Authored parameters for the shared ground-forager program. food_tag invertebrate matches the largest diet share; the default rest window (sun 10-90 degrees) keeps a nocturnal animal resting through the day; flee/food radii are judgement for a medium, urban-tolerant omnivore.
